questions_and_answers.question_text: What are the four meanings of rénjia?
When rénjia means "I," what is the speaker being?
What do lǐ and mào literally mean?
Write the Chinese for "I've been waiting for you for an hour," using rénjia.

answers.answer_text: Rénjia děng nǐ yíge zhōngtóu le.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "People say that place is very pretty."

answers.answer_text: Rénjia dōu shuō nèige dìfang hěn hǎo kàn.
Politeness of speech, saying the right things at the right times, table manners, and so on.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Today's Sunday. Let me sleep a little later!"

answers.answer_text: Jīntian shi Xīngqītiān, ràng rénjia duō shuì yìhuǐr ma!

articles.text:
6. A: Rénjia dōu juéde Xiǎo Wáng    Everyone feels Xiǎo Wáng is a very
      shi ge hěn yǒu lǐmàode háizi. well-mannered child.

Notes on No. 6

rénjia: This pronoun has a FEW DIFFERENT MEANINGS.

(1) "everyone, people (in general), they":
Rénjia dōu shuō nèige dìfang     People say that place is very pretty.
hěn hǎo kàn.

(2) "other people" or "someone else":
Zhèiběnr shū dàgài kěyi jiè gěi  I can probably lend you this book, but
ni, búguò shi rénjiade, wǒ děi   it's someone else's. I have to ask
xiān wènwen.                     them first.

(3) A SPECIFIC third party — "he," "she," or "they":
Rénjia bù jiè, suàn le ba!       If he doesn't want to lend it, then
                                 just forget it!
Nǐ kàn rénjia Xiǎo Huá xuéde     Look at how well Xiǎo Huá does in her
duō hǎo, nǐ ne!                  studies, but you!

(4) Rénjia may also refer to THE SPEAKER — in other words, "I." In such a case, the speaker is being intentionally PLAYFUL, WITTY, or CUTE:

Nǐ yào zhème duō?! Gěi rénjia    You want so much?! Come on, give me
yìdiǎnr ma!                      a little!
Rénjia děng nǐ yíge zhōngtóu le. I've been waiting for you for an hour.
Jīntian shi Xīngqītiān, ràng     Today's Sunday. Let me sleep a little
rénjia duō shuì yìhuǐr ma!       later!

lǐmào: "manners, etiquette," the expression in speech and behavior of MODESTY and RESPECTFULNESS. This includes politeness of speech, saying the right things at the right times, table manners, and so on. (Lǐ is "ritual." Mào is "appearance.")

Yǒu lǐmào means "to be well-mannered," méiyou lǐmào "to be ill-mannered."
